extracted.intended_audience: Researchers (authors and reviewers) in biology and medicine considering submission to or participation in eLife peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Policy describing eLife's approach to peer review: what is reviewed (preprints), how decisions are made, what outputs are produced, and standards for requests to authors. Intended to guide editors, reviewers and authors about eLife's procedures and expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only review research papers available as preprints
rubrics_metrics.description: "we only review research papers that have been made available as preprints"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife's system requires that articles be posted as preprints before they are peer reviewed by eLife; this is intended to combine the immediacy and openness of a preprint with peer review and curation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions made by editors who are active researchers
rubrics_metrics.description: "all decisions are made by editors who are active researchers"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions are taken by practicing researchers (not professional editors detached from research), implying subject-matter expertise in decision-making about manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No artificial limit on the number of articles / no set acceptance rate
rubrics_metrics.description: "we do not artificially limit the number of articles we publish or have a set acceptance rate"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance is determined by merit under the policy rather than by quotas or target acceptance rates; editorial selection is driven by the quality of work rather than numerical targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors and reviewers discuss reviews before decision
rubrics_metrics.description: "editors and reviewers discuss their reviews with each other before reaching a decision on a manuscript"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is a deliberative process: reviewers and editors exchange views to reach a consensus decision rather than acting on isolated reports; this supports coherent editorial outcomes and shared understanding of required revisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for extra experiments or analyses only if essential and time-reasonable
rubrics_metrics.description: "extra experiments, analyses, or data collection are only requested if they are essential and can be reasonably completed within about two months"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should limit requests to those strictly necessary to support the claims and achievable in a short timeframe (~2 months). This aims to avoid overburdening authors with extensive additional work and to keep review timely; see related guidance on COVID-19 publishing timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce public comments evaluating strengths, weaknesses, and whether claims are justified by data
rubrics_metrics.description: "public comments from the peer reviewers on the strengths and weaknesses of the work, and whether the authors’ claims and conclusions are justified by their data, that can be posted alongside the preprint"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer reviewers provide a publicly visible evaluation summary and individual reviews that state major conclusions, identify strengths and weaknesses, and explicitly assess whether conclusions are supported by the data. These public comments are intended for readers and other interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed feedback to authors to support revision and improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: "detailed feedback on the manuscript for the authors, including requests for revisions and suggestions for improvement"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In addition to public comments, reviewers provide private/detailed guidance aimed at helping authors revise the preprint; when revised preprints are accepted, that detailed feedback is published as part of the paper together with the author response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish evaluation summary and public reviews alongside preprint
rubrics_metrics.description: "The public comments include an evaluation summary that captures the major conclusions of the review process, and public reviews from each of the peer reviewers that outline the strengths and weaknesses of the manuscript."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency standard: the public record should include both a concise evaluation summary capturing major conclusions and each reviewer's full public review so readers can see the basis for assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted manuscripts include decision letter and author responses publication
rubrics_metrics.description: "accepted manuscripts published in eLife include the decision letter from the editor to the authors, and the author responses to the decision letter"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For accepted papers eLife publishes the editorial decision letter and the authors' responses to it, increasing transparency about the revision process and editorial reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess research primarily on peer reviews rather than journal title
rubrics_metrics.description: "research is primarily assessed on the basis of reviews from peers and not on the title of the journal in which it was published"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation philosophy: focus on the content and peer assessments rather than journal brand; supports fairer assessment of work by emphasizing expert commentary over publication venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for peer review that is faster, fairer and more open
rubrics_metrics.description: "The overall aim is to make peer review faster, fairer and more open."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level objective guiding all process choices (preprint-first, limited experimental demands, transparent publishing of reviews and responses, active-researcher editors) to improve speed, fairness and openness of peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject reliance on Impact Factor; endorse DORA principles
rubrics_metrics.description: "eLife does not support the Impact Factor and is a co-founder of the Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy stance against using Journal Impact Factor as a measure of research quality; alignment with DORA implies commitment to more responsible research assessment practices (e.g., evaluating the content and merits of individual works).
